## Overview

Scoring a cyber range cannot trust what guests report: the agent owns the attack box from the first prompt and owns each target it compromises. Evidence is the record captured **outside every VM**: per-segment packet captures taken on the bridges, serial consoles, the realization stage stream, readiness and verification results, daemon session continuity, and exported in-guest telemetry. It streams off the sample as it is generated, so the record received before a compromise cannot be rewritten afterward.

Scoring consumes the record through the oracle's read-only accessors: [Custom Goals](goals.qmd#the-oracle-surface) covers reading it from a goal type, and [Corroborating Against Evidence](goals.qmd#corroborating-against-evidence) is the worked pattern.

Evidence is on by default inside an eval: when a sample runs under Inspect, the provider derives a location beside the eval log and records automatically. Outside an eval context (CLI experiments, batteries), set `INSPECT_RANGES_EVIDENCE_SINK` to enable it; with neither, evidence is off and one INFO line says so.

## Captured Streams

| Stream | Contents |
|---|---|
| `pcap/<segment>` | One packet capture per bridge, full snaplen, rotated and shipped live. It runs in a `NET_RAW`-only sidecar sharing the range's network namespace, so nothing is added to any guest. |
| `console/<guest>` | Each guest's serial console, streamed continuously (not only on failure). |
| `capture-stderr/<segment>` | The capture tool's own diagnostics, including the kernel-drop summaries tcpdump prints on exit. |
| `stages`, `verify` | The realization stage stream (with host emit clocks) and the readiness/verification results. |
| `session` | Daemon session pins and re-pins: a guest daemon restart is itself evidence. |
| `telemetry/<collector>`, `telemetry-meta/<collector>` | Exported in-guest telemetry deltas and the per-poll watermark records that make coverage decidable (below). |
| `exec/<guest>`, `exec-meta/<guest>` | The exec witness: every `execve` on a Linux guest (pid, ppid, uid, argv, host-ingest timestamp), with per-poll coverage records so "no events" vs "witness dead" is decidable. A Windows guest or a connector-less kernel gets one declared `unsupported` record. It accepts only kernel-originated messages, so an in-guest process cannot forge records. No shipped goal reads it; custom goals may, through the oracle's `exec_events()`. |
| `draws` | The per-sample variable draw seed and values (non-secret by construction), so recorded samples re-derive post-hoc. |
| `plants` | What challenge setup planted where (tokens, flags), timestamped: the scorer's proof-contract record. |
| `probe/<goal id>` | The nonce-bound active prober's transcript for goals that use it. |
| `terminal/<session>` | The agent's terminal sessions when the task wires the [terminal](challenges.qmd#terminal-sessions) tool: the pane output re-encoded as UTF-8, host-timestamped. A pane the agent adds with `tmux new-window` or `split-window` records to its own `terminal/<session>.p<N>` stream. At close, an asciicast assembled from each stream lands beside a local evidence location as `terminal-<session>.cast` (panes as `terminal-<session>.p<N>.cast`; a remote location carries the streams but gets no cast files). |
| `heartbeat`, `clock` | Capture liveness and watermarks for our own collectors, and wall-clock anomaly records. |

## Storage

The per-sample location is derived, never configured per sample:

```
<evallogstem>.evidence/<sample_id>_<epoch>_<attempt>/
```

Local beside a local log in development; in the log's S3 bucket when the log dir is `s3://`. Durability inherits from the log location, and anything that finds the log finds the evidence. Each attempt gets a fresh prefix, so retries never rewrite an earlier attempt's record. `INSPECT_RANGES_EVIDENCE_SINK` overrides the base for deployments whose evidence needs a different bucket or retention than their logs.

At finalize, the sample's Inspect store receives the binding under `inspect_ranges:evidence`: the evidence pointer, each writer's seal digest, and the per-stream chain heads. The same values are mirrored to an INFO log line, which is all that remains if the sample context is gone by teardown time (deferred teardown, `cleanup=False`).

## Tamper Evidence

Collectors in the range container are trusted **while the instance is uncompromised**, and their output is preserved off-instance as it streams. The record itself is tamper-evident by format: write-once chunks, a per-stream hash chain over every record's full metadata, explicit in-chain gap records, and a terminal seal per writer binding chain heads and counts.

The format's guarantee has an exact scope. Everything **at or below the seal** is tamper-evident from the location alone: any rewrite, reorder, deletion, or hole breaks the chain, and `evidence verify` names the first break. The **seal tier itself** (its fields, its presence, the record's location, the writer set) is anchored only by the seal digest held outside the record, which is what the sample-store binding provides: run `evidence verify --expect-seal` with the binding's digests and the full claim holds. A writer the binding does not name is itself a break, so additions are detected, not just mutations. Without a binding, verify attests internal consistency only, and an **unsealed** record is extendable as well as truncatable. The lifecycle makes unsealed-at-rest an anomaly: finalize seals the record, and the independent reaper ([Operations](cli.qmd#reaper)) seals abandoned records, so even a `kill -9` of the driver leaves a verifiable record of everything streamed before the kill.

Two bounded windows are part of the design and visible in the record rather than silent:

- **Backpressure is never silent.** When the local buffer cap is hit, the oldest unstreamed chunk is dropped and an explicit gap record joins the chain in sequence, with a named cause (`buffer-cap`, `capture-restart`, `poll-failed`, and the like). Scoring's completeness checks see the gaps.
- **Manifest batching has a crash window.** Chunks deliver on every flush, but manifest parts are cut on a bounded cadence (15 s or 256 records, and always at seal). A crash can leave up to one interval of records whose chunks survive as unreferenced residue; the record never claims the missing window.

## Telemetry Export

Scenario telemetry (journald, application logs, EDR event files) lives inside guests because defenders are supposed to see it. The exporter polls declared collectors through the existing control-channel verbs on a cadence and ships each poll's delta, with a watermark record per poll. The export path is the vsock control plane: nothing in-range can observe or firewall it, and the range's network isolation is never punctured.

The assurance claim: **export upgrades the timeline, not the source.** Pre-compromise telemetry becomes immutable once streamed. Producer silencing shows as a watermark stall, an unreachable guest as poll-gap records, log truncation or rewrite as a watermark regression. All three are decidable from the sealed record alone, and all three are distinct from "no events". The read itself remains a guest read: a compromised host can forge what it exports from the moment it falls, which is why detection-type goals consume the watermarks as a completeness precondition rather than treating exported content as proof.

Operational note: the guest daemon reaps each command's process group when the command returns, so an in-guest background producer started over the channel must detach with `setsid` to outlive its starting exec.

## Exec Witness {#the-exec-witness}

The guest daemon can witness every `execve` on a Linux guest and the host ships the events to `exec/<guest>`: pid, parent, uid, argv (sanitized, byte-capped), and a host-ingest timestamp. The subscriber is lazy-armed by the host's first poll, so builds never activate it, and `INSPECT_RANGES_EXEC_WITNESS=0` disables it completely with no image rebuild. The stream is record-only and carries the same guest-tier assurance as telemetry export: the pre-compromise timeline is immutable once streamed, and a Windows guest or a kernel without the connector gets one declared `unsupported` record.

Loss is always a gap, never silent, but its size is known only when the kernel tells us: a ring overwrite (`exec-ring-overflow`) carries the exact count, while a kernel subscriber overflow (`exec-subscriber-loss`) is recorded as an *unknown-size* gap. Coverage is decidable from the per-poll records on `exec-meta/<guest>`, and a daemon restart is detected from a change in the daemon's boot session carried on every reply.

Trust boundary: the witness accepts only genuine kernel connector messages (sender `nl_pid` 0), so an in-guest process — even as root — cannot inject forged `execve` records. A root process can still *blind* the witness by killing the daemon, but that shows as poll-failure and restart gaps, never as silent loss; and since the daemon runs unprivileged by default, an agent must first earn root (itself witnessed) before it can interfere at all.

## Verifying a Record

```{.bash .fragment}
# internal consistency: replay every chain, report coverage and gaps
inspect-ranges evidence verify ./logs/mytask.evidence/sample1_1_1

# the full guarantee: anchor each writer's seal to its digest from
# the eval log's binding (store key inspect_ranges:evidence); the
# digests are bare hex, exactly as the binding and INFO line show
inspect-ranges evidence verify \
  s3://bucket/logs/run.evidence/sample1_1_1 \
  --expect-seal driver=4f8b21... --expect-seal host=9d03ce...
```

Output names the first chain break with its neighborhood, per-stream coverage spans, the gap inventory, and each seal's claimed lease and sample ids; `--json` emits the report for tooling. Exit status is 0 only when every chain replays and every supplied binding matches. Timestamps come from both clocks: capture records carry the range host's clocks, driver records carry the driver's, and paired records around stage reports bound the offset between them, so cross-clock comparisons carry a tolerance.

## Deployment Guidance {#deployment-guidance-store-side-prevention}

The format detects tampering; preventing it is the store's job, and the writer already helps: on S3 every put is conditional (`If-None-Match: *`), so rewrites of delivered objects are refused with a 412. To make the store refuse unconditional rewrites from **any** writer holding the credential, apply a bucket policy denying `s3:PutObject` without the conditional header; Object Lock is the stricter alternative where retention rules demand it. Grant the capture host put-only credentials; the writer never reads back.

Local evidence (a local log dir, no override) is fine for development and does not survive instance compromise: for untrusted-model runs, point the log dir or the sink override at off-instance storage. `inspect-ranges doctor` warns about this in its Evidence group.

## Environment Vars

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `INSPECT_RANGES_EVIDENCE_SINK` | unset | Override base for evidence locations; unset derives from the eval log location (the default and the recommendation). Also enables evidence outside an eval context. |
| `INSPECT_RANGES_EVIDENCE_BUFFER_MB` | 64 | Per-writer in-memory buffer cap; past it the oldest unstreamed chunk drops with an in-chain gap record. Joins the sample's admission memory charge. |
| `INSPECT_RANGES_EVIDENCE_MAX_MB` | 4096 | Per-writer volume cap (a sample has at most two writers: `driver` and `host`). Breach yields in-chain `evidence-cap` gaps and an `incomplete` seal, never a failed sample. |
| `INSPECT_RANGES_EXEC_WITNESS` | unset (on) | Set `0` to disable the exec witness: the per-guest poller is never constructed, so the in-guest subscriber never arms (lazy-arm makes this the complete kill switch, no image rebuild involved). |
| `INSPECT_RANGES_CAST_STORE_CAP_MB` | 50 | Per-session cap on the asciicast copy written into the sample store (and so into the eval log) for viewer playback; an over-cap cast keeps its tail with a marker noting the cut, and the evidence copy stays complete. |
| `CAPTURE_CHUNK_MB`, `CAPTURE_CAP_MB`, `CAPTURE_MAX_RESTARTS` | 10 / 2048 / 5 | Capture sidecar tuning, read from the environment at `up`: rotation chunk size, per-segment disk cap, tcpdump restart budget. |

The finalize flush budget (30 seconds) and the manifest batching cadence (15 seconds / 256 records) are constants: teardown is never hostage to a slow uplink, and what cannot flush inside the budget is recorded in the seal rather than silently dropped.

Evidence never destabilizes the sample it observes: a sink that cannot open, a knob that cannot parse, or a mid-run delivery failure disables or gaps the record with loud logging, and the sample proceeds and scores normally.
